findings.subject: NCT05259917
findings.R_source_quote: This publication outlines the rigorous, multi-factorial approach used to design a phase 3 trial with an optimized, patient- and physician-preferred measure to assess measure efficacy, and discusses reasons for the superiority of the selected primary endpoint over other potential measures
findings.R_object_value: patient- and physician-preferred measure optimized for efficacy assessment
findings.f_method: Identify which registered endpoint occupies the success-determining slot for THIS catalyst (the registered PRIMARY whose timeFrame aligns with the catalyst readout), then test whether the marketed success-basis endpoint is that one. Two axes are independent: efficacy-vs-safety (what it measures) and primary-vs-secondary (its hierarchy slot). A secondary endpoint can be a legitimate efficacy endpoint — describing one is NOT masking. Also inspect version HISTORY for a CONSTRUCT/TYPE change of the registered primary near readout.
findings.rationale: The claim describes the registered primary endpoint (PGI-C time to beginning of symptom relief) as optimized for efficacy assessment. M shows this primary endpoint has remained unchanged since trial registration (version 0, 2022-02-28) with no construct changes in primary_endpoint_timeline. The claim is characterizing the registered primary itself, not substituting a secondary endpoint into the success-determining slot.
findings.m_evidence: primary_endpoint_timeline shows only one version (version 0, date 2022-02-28) with primary 'Time to beginning of symptom relief Patient Global Impression of Change (PGI-C)' and timeFrame 'within 12 hours of the first investigational medicinal product (IMP) administration.' No construct or type changes observed.

findings.rationale: The claim asserts sebetralstat is the 'first potential oral, on-demand treatment for hereditary angioedema.' The rule targets naive cross-trial efficacy comparisons; no efficacy superiority claim is made here that would invoke the rule's predicate.
